testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to make a lane change, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during the driving test, check your mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and smoothly move into the other lane only when it is safe.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with the vehicle's belts?
questions.explanation: Check all belts to make sure they are tight and not worn. Learn how much movement is normal for each belt.

questions.question: In cool weather, when ice begins to melt as the temperature rises, what happens to the road?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive on.

questions.explanation: When ice starts to melt, water sits on top of the ice. This makes the road even more slippery. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning light turns on while you are driving?

options.text: Stop and park where you are.
Leave the road safely as soon as possible and park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road safely as soon as possible and park.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving, safely exit the road and park your vehicle. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread.
questions.explanation: Good tire tread helps prevent hydroplaning on wet roads. Worn tires and low tire pressure increase the risk of hydroplaning. If you start to hydroplane, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used on rear tires.
Yes, if the load is light.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Yawning often or rubbing your eyes.

questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, drifting from your lane, missing exits, and feeling irritable. Staying in your lane is normal, safe driving.

questions.question: When planning to change lanes, how often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Check them as you normally would.
Check them more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors as part of normal driving. When changing lanes, check them even more frequently.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should you accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always a good habit.
To keep control of your vehicle.
To stay behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When driving on slippery surfaces, accelerate very slowly. Using too much power can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Where should the center of gravity be in a trailer?

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Load cargo as low as possible in the trailer. A center of gravity that is too high increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully through work zones. Slow down when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is:

options.text: Illegal to transport in most states.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable. It has a high center of gravity, and the meat can swing, which makes the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always come to a complete stop.
May need to swerve your vehicle out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve your vehicle out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you don't have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: When starting an engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Place the engine in first gear.

questions.explanation: After starting the engine during your pre-trip inspection, listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tires with 3/32 inch of tread

questions.explanation: All tires on a vehicle must be the same size. Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread. Tires can be made by different manufacturers.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum weight of a fully loaded vehicle as set by the manufacturer
The weight rating of a tire
The weight rating per axle for a combination vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight of a fully loaded vehicle as set by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight set by the manufacturer for a fully loaded vehicle.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Only happens at very high speeds.
Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
Happens most when tire pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is more likely if tire pressure is too low or if tread is worn.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system if they build up. Air tank drain valves remove this water and oil.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, weight should be:

options.text: Placed as far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Cargo with a low center of gravity is less likely to tip over. Always place weight as low as possible.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes with the report.
Read the report first when you do your inspection.
Skip your inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report first when you do your inspection.
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to read any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:

options.text: Rubbing against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check that exhaust system parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against moving parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope the problem goes away.
Write a report describing your concerns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, you may need to write a report on the vehicle. Write down any problems that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What does an air compressor do in an air brake system?

options.text: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
It moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: It pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls it.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to make the brakes work.

questions.question: When checking your tires during a pre-trip inspection, you should look at:
questions.explanation: Check that your tire pressure is not too low or too high.

questions.question: While driving, mirrors should be checked:

options.text: Only when there may be a problem.

questions.explanation: Know what is around your vehicle at all times. Make it a habit to check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.explanation: Check your gauges before starting. After you start the engine, coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating range.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, block the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: If you need to stop on the road to unload cargo, you should:

options.text: Stop suddenly, since you are already on the road.
Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
Wave your arm out the window to get other drivers' attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your brake lights to warn other drivers when you plan to slow or stop somewhere they may not expect it. Use this method when stopping on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Is caused only by physical distractions.
Gets worse if you pre-program radio stations.
Can be prevented by avoiding conversation with others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be prevented by avoiding conversation with others.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for objects), mental (like talking with passengers), or both (like texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving, pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: When checking your vehicle, make sure your dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When checking your mirrors:

options.text: Do not use the passenger side mirror.
Do not use the driver's side mirror.
Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors on both sides of your vehicle often while driving. It is important to know what is behind and beside your vehicle.

questions.question: Do not shift gears based on:

options.text: The actions of the vehicle next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The actions of the vehicle next to you.
questions.explanation: Learn your vehicle's engine rpm range to know when to shift gears. Shift up when your engine reaches the top of that range. You can also learn which speeds work best for each gear and shift based on your speedometer.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is near idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is near idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is near idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is near idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal gradually to stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is near idle.

questions.question: Alcohol can be removed from your system:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol on its own.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting a vehicle?
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level in seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: If brakes create too much heat:

options.text: The brakes may squeak more than usual.

questions.explanation: Brakes can handle a lot of heat, but do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Brakes can fade and lose stopping power if they get too hot. Also use engine braking to slow down.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure causes a loud bang sound and heavy thumping or vibration. Heavy steering or fishtailing are signs of tire problems. Smoother steering is not a sign of tire failure.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to keep driving. Caffeine is not a safe solution.

questions.question: Containerized loads are used:

options.text: When cargo is too large for a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight travels by rail or ship. Drivers must check that containers do not exceed safe and legal weight limits.

questions.question: Texting while operating a CMV is:
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and illegal. You cannot text while operating a CMV under any circumstances.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on vehicle speed, vehicle weight, and road surface traction.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Always shift into a lower gear before going downhill. This prevents you from overusing your brakes.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
Is not encouraged because it distracts you.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Always watch ahead for hazards. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts indicates the nuts may be loose. Check that they are tight before driving.

questions.question: Once air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Begin pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor when air pressure reaches about 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure happens from loss of pressure or overuse on hills causing brake fade. Downshifting does not cause hydraulic brake failure.
